claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Friday, April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET.
The splashdown was a parachute-assisted landing.
The splashdown concluded a 10-day mission around the moon.
The crew returned home for recovery by U.S. Navy and NASA teams.
The Artemis II Orion capsule re-entered Earth's atmosphere at roughly 25,000 mph.
The Artemis II Orion capsule utilized drogue chutes and then three main parachutes.
The parachutes slowed the capsule to about 30 km/h for the final splashdown.
Inflatable bags were deployed following the splashdown to ensure the capsule remained upright.
Recovery crews were on standby following the splashdown.
Recovery crews aimed to get the crew out of the capsule within approximately two hours.
The Artemis II crew members are Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen
